facts.statement: The genus Sclerorhynchus was first described by Woodward in 1889.
The type species of the genus is Sclerorhynchus atavus.
Other known species include S. leptodon, S. pettersi, S. fanninensis, S. priscus, and S. karakensis.
facts.quote: subdivision: †Sclerorhynchus leptodon (Arambourg, 1935) †Sclerorhynchus pettersi Case & Cappetta, 1997 †Sclerorhynchus fanninensis Cappetta & Case, 1999 †Sclerorhynchus priscus Cappetta & Case, 1999 †Sclerorhynchus karakensis Mustafa, Case, & Zalmout, 2002

facts.statement: The genus Ganopristis is now treated as a junior synonym of Sclerorhynchus.
facts.quote: The genus Ganopristis is considered a junior synonym of Sclerorhynchus.

facts.statement: The time range for Sclerorhynchus spans from the Cenomanian to the Maastrichtian, between 100.5 and 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Cenomanian to Maastrichtian (100.5 to 66 million years ago)

facts.statement: Sclerorhynchus belongs to the class Chondrichthyes.
Sclerorhynchus is classified within the family Sclerorhynchidae.
Fossils of Sclerorhynchus have been found in the Middle East, North Africa, Europe, and North America.
facts.quote: It was a widespread genus, with fossils found in the Middle East (S. atavus, S. karakensis), North Africa (S. leptodon), Europe (S. leptodon), and North America (S. fanninensis, S. pettersi, S. priscus).
